description: Ship at minimum two fixture TS projects under `bas/fixtures/` (`ts-junk-drawer/` and `ts-jsdoc-tags/`) each with hand-curated `expected-graph.json`. CI fails if any fixture's extracted graph diverges byte-for-byte from the expected file. The `ts-jsdoc-tags/` fixture pins the leading-comment contract that `react-component-library` depends on.

requirements.description: Ship at minimum two TypeScript fixture projects under bas/fixtures/: ts-junk-drawer/ (general TS constructs) and ts-jsdoc-tags/ (JSDoc and annotation coverage). Each fixture must include hand-curated expected-graph.json files. CI must run Extract against each fixture and perform a byte-for-byte comparison against the expected-graph.json. Any divergence must fail the CI build. The ts-jsdoc-tags/ fixture specifically pins the leading-comment contract required by react-component-library. Fixture projects must be self-contained (no external network dependencies) and must not evolve without an accompanying expected-graph.json update.
requirements.title: Golden-Fixture Determinism Gate in CI

validation.notes: Test that the fixture comparison utility correctly identifies byte differences between two JSON files
Test that expected-graph.json files are valid JSON and conform to the Graph proto schema
TCG-GOLDEN-FIXTURE: CI extracts ts-junk-drawer fixture and asserts byte-for-byte match with expected-graph.json
TCG-GOLDEN-JSDOC: CI extracts ts-jsdoc-tags fixture and asserts byte-for-byte match with expected-graph.json; specifically validates leading_comments fields
CI fails with a diff output when expected-graph.json does not match actual extraction
Extraction from a clean git clone (no build artifacts) produces identical expected-graph.json output
ts-jsdoc-tags expected-graph.json is signed off by react-component-library team as matching their annotation requirements
CI gate blocks merges that unintentionally change graph extraction behavior
